1. High: incremental task checkpoints don’t serialize the envelope the POC plan calls for. The plan says each `incremental/__list` entry should be JSON containing `{type, tool_use_id, timestamp, data}` so gmeta preserves the same semantics as v1 ([docs/gmeta-poc-plan.md:103](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/docs/gmeta-poc-plan.md#L103), [docs/gmeta-poc-plan.md:123](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/docs/gmeta-poc-plan.md#L123)). In the implementation, the gmeta path writes only the redacted raw `IncrementalData` blob and drops `IncrementalType`, `ToolUseID`, and timestamp entirely ([gmeta_store.go:341](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store.go#L341)). That is a real data loss regression relative to v1, which still records the full envelope ([committed.go:188](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/committed.go#L188)). The new test only checks that an entry exists, not that its content is shaped correctly ([gmeta_store_test.go:298](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store_test.go#L298)).

2. Medium: `session/ids` does not reliably preserve append order, but the read path assumes it does. The plan explicitly treats `session/ids` as the ordered source of truth for session ordering ([docs/gmeta-poc-plan.md:47](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/docs/gmeta-poc-plan.md#L47), [docs/gmeta-poc-plan.md:73](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/docs/gmeta-poc-plan.md#L73)). Here, list entry names are generated from `time.Now().UnixMilli()` plus a hash suffix ([gmeta_store.go:182](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store.go#L182)), and `GetSessionLog` later picks the “latest” session by taking the last lexicographically sorted list entry ([gmeta_store.go:765](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store.go#L765), [gmeta_store.go:863](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store.go#L863)). If two sessions are appended in the same millisecond, or writes come from skewed clocks, ordering falls back to the hash suffix rather than append order, so resume/log lookup can pick the wrong session. The current interop test masks this by sorting the observed IDs before asserting ([gmeta_interop_test.go:212](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_interop_test.go#L212)).

I didn’t find other obvious plan mismatches in the wiring: condensation, stop finalization, attach, and migrate are all hooked up as intended.
